findings.issue: AC-1 HTTP test is mislabelled and does NOT cover the actual AC-1 requirement. The spec AC-1 says: caller holds NO {mgmt_object:agent, create, scope} grant → 403, zero employee rows, zero Keycloak calls. The test at line 501 labelled 'AC-1' only verifies the MISSING HEADER path (401/UNAUTHENTICATED), not the NO-GRANT path (403/no_mgmt_grant). There is no HTTP integration test that exercises a caller who is authenticated (has an x-dev-user header and a valid employee) but lacks the mgmt_object:agent grant. makeFakePool only has isGenesisOwner: true in all HTTP describe blocks — the 403 path is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add a test with isGenesisOwner: false in makeFakePool (and adminGrants=[] via the fake pool returning empty rows for the mgmt_object:% query). Send a valid x-dev-user header; assert response is 403 and fakeKc.created.length === 0.

findings.issue: AC-3 (scope narrowing: hire rejected when target position is outside admin's org-scope) has zero HTTP integration coverage. The ADR §1 step 2 and spec AC-3 both require this case to be tested. No test in agent-hire.test.ts exercises a non-genesis admin whose grant covers department D1 but the target position_id is in department D2.
findings.suggestion: Add an HTTP integration test with a non-genesis admin pool (isGenesisOwner: false, adminGrants covering one dept, position returning a disjoint dept). Assert 403 and zero KC calls. The makeFakePool's department_id return in the position lookup can be made configurable.

findings.issue: SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id = '${tenantId}' uses string interpolation inside the SQL text. The tenantId is already UUID-validated by assertUuidShape() immediately before withTenantTx is called, so injection is not possible in practice; however, the grants.ts precedent (which this file is supposed to mirror) uses the same pattern and is accepted project-wide. This is a nit for style consistency — the SET LOCAL pattern cannot use parameterized queries in PostgreSQL anyway.
findings.suggestion: No change required (matches existing grants.ts pattern). Document the assertUuidShape pre-check as the invariant that makes this safe.

findings.issue: getAdminToken error propagates the raw KC response body in the error message: 'KC admin token failed: ${resp.status} ${resp.body}'. This error is caught in agents.ts and surfaced as a 503 response to the caller. The KC response body is Keycloak's error payload (e.g. {error: 'invalid_client', error_description: '...'}), which does not contain the admin credential itself, but could reveal internal error details. This is acceptable for dev; for production, it should be scrubbed to a generic message before surfacing to callers.
findings.suggestion: Nit only (dev scope). Consider wrapping the KC error to strip the response body before surfacing in HTTP 503: 'Keycloak service account creation failed' (generic). The full error can remain in a server-side log.
